entrypoints.summary: Extraction of an attacker-crafted SquashFS (.squashfs or .sfs) archive invokes the registered SquashFS handler and its fragment read path.

affected_components.role: The parser reads the serialized Offset field and ReadBlock checks and uses it in cache-buffer pointer arithmetic.

causal_paths.kind: serialized inode offset to cache memcpy

code_slices.fixed: Not inspected: the supplied 26.01 source is a compressed archive and no clean source diff is available in this bundle.
code_slices.surrounding_context: The report identifies Parse4 as reading Offset directly from the regular-file inode and states that Open2 does not constrain it below the archive block size.
code_slices.vulnerable: ReadBlock assigns node.Offset to offsetInBlock, tests offsetInBlock + blockSize against _cachedUnpackBlockSize, and then copies from _cachedBlock + offsetInBlock.

negative_controls: On a 64-bit build, widened arithmetic causes the bounds check to reject the crafted request.
observability.positive_marker: The report records a heap-buffer-overflow at SquashfsHandler.cpp:2198 reading before an 8192-byte allocation, and describes bytes preceding the cache buffer appearing in extracted output.

preconditions: A 32-bit 7-Zip build with 32-bit size_t is used.
The target extracts an attacker-crafted SquashFS archive; the report states 64-bit builds reject the same overflowing range.

trigger_steps.payload_shape: A fragment-backed file inode with a near-maximum UInt32 Offset, such as 0xFFFFFFFC or the report's 0xFFFF8000 arithmetic example, and a small file size selected to wrap offset plus size.
trigger_steps.summary: Generate a SquashFS v4 image with a regular-file inode carrying a large fragment Offset and request extraction of its file.

capabilities.concept: out-of-bounds read before cached fragment buffer

impacts.concept: heap memory disclosure through extracted file

relation_candidates.rationale: The inode Offset reaches offsetInBlock, and a large value can make the checked addition wrap on 32-bit builds.

relation_candidates.dst: out-of-bounds read before cached fragment buffer
relation_candidates.rationale: Bypassing the wrapped range guard permits memcpy to use the wrapped cache-base-plus-offset pointer.

relation_candidates.dst: heap memory disclosure through extracted file
relation_candidates.rationale: The report states that memcpy reads bytes before the cache allocation and writes them into the extracted file.
relation_candidates.src: out-of-bounds read before cached fragment buffer

relation_candidates.rationale: A non-wrapping representability and bounds predicate would reject the crafted out-of-range fragment request; exact 26.01 implementation details require source-archive decoding and diff review.

impact.affected_asset: Heap-resident data preceding the SquashFS handler's cached unpack buffer.
impact.attacker_capability: An actor who can cause extraction of a crafted SquashFS file can select a wrapped fragment offset and obtain copied bytes preceding the handler cache allocation in the extracted output.
impact.security_effect: Heap information disclosure during archive extraction on 32-bit builds.

causal_trace.summary: A crafted regular-file inode supplies a full 32-bit on-disk Offset that is parsed into node.Offset; the report's generator places the attacker-selected value in the inode.

On a 32-bit build, assigning node.Offset to offsetInBlock and checking offsetInBlock + blockSize against _cachedUnpackBlockSize permits modular unsigned wraparound, so an offset-plus-length range outside the cached block can appear in range.
After the wrapped check is bypassed, cache-base-plus-offset pointer arithmetic wraps backward and memcpy reads from before _cachedBlock.

The bytes preceding the cache allocation are copied into the extracted file, creating an in-band heap-information disclosure on affected 32-bit builds; the report documents an ASan heap-buffer-overflow at ReadBlock line 2198.

primary_invariant.statement: Before copying a fragment, the requested range [offsetInBlock, offsetInBlock + blockSize) must be representable without wraparound and wholly lie within the cached unpacked block.
primary_invariant.violated_because: The guard compares a wrapped 32-bit offsetInBlock + blockSize result with _cachedUnpackBlockSize; therefore a large serialized offset can evade rejection on 32-bit builds, and the following base-plus-offset computation addresses memory before the cache.

quality.review_notes: The primary public disclosure supplies the serialized input construction, arithmetic example, affected code, 32-bit/64-bit contrast, and an ASan trace. The ASan trace is report-provided observed evidence, not an independently executed run. The 26.01 source archive is present but compressed and was not decoded; consequently, exact per-finding patch semantics remain unverified.

remediation.invariant_restored: The fixed release should reject fragment offsets and lengths whose sum cannot be represented or whose range lies outside the cached block; the supplied fixed source archive was not decoded and diffed, so the exact implementation is not verified here.

state_context.attacker_state_setup: Craft a SquashFS v4 image whose regular-file inode references a fragment and contains a large Offset value paired with a small file size; exercise extraction on a 32-bit build.
data_structure_invariants: node.Offset and the requested file portion must define a range inside the cached unpacked fragment block.
The offset-plus-length calculation and cache-base-plus-offset calculation must not wrap.

numeric_domains.attacker_constraints: Serialized as the full UInt32 Offset field of a SquashFS regular-file inode.
numeric_domains.name: node.Offset / offsetInBlock

numeric_domains.attacker_constraints: Derived from the file size and reported as controllable through FileSize up to the archive block size.
numeric_domains.name: blockSize

state_context.state_machine: A SquashFS regular-file inode is parsed, the extraction path requests its fragment, ReadBlock validates the requested portion against the cached decompressed block, and the resulting bytes are copied to extraction output.

target.component: SquashFS archive handler, CHandler::ReadBlock in CPP/7zip/Archive/SquashfsHandler.cpp

oracle.expected_negative: The same offset-plus-length input is rejected on a 64-bit build because the addition is widened and does not wrap.
oracle.expected_positive: On a 32-bit build, extracting the crafted SquashFS input reaches ReadBlock's memcpy with a wrapped cache pointer and produces an ASan heap-buffer-overflow; exposed bytes are directed to extraction output.
